page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor family. The server provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 128.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 67 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, operates without hardware GPU accelerators, and does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions.

Benchmark evaluations indicate exceptional memory subsystem performance. Memory bandwidth benchmarks place the instance in the top 10% tier, achieving 386.95 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB read operations and 184.61 GB/sec for write operations, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3312.35. Compute performance reflects high parallel execution efficiency, evidenced by a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21327.0 and strong results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 335.85 GB/sec and Clang compilation at 48415.0. In contrast, single-core metrics—such as stress-ng single-core (1706.49) and Geekbench single-core (1809.0)—fall within average ranges.

Database and I/O-intensive application metrics demonstrate significant capacity, with PassMark database operations reaching 47436.59 (top 10% tier) and Redis SET operations processing 65.82 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput is measured at 67.54 GB/sec. Specialized workloads such as large language model inference show mixed behavior on CPU execution: 7B text generation performs well at 28.94 tokens per second, but 70B prompt processing is limited to 5.9 tokens per second, reflecting the absence of dedicated GPU acceleration.

The architecture delivers high multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth per allocated resource, making it an efficient choice for scale-out workloads. The m8gb.8xlarge is suited for transactional and in-memory databases, web serving tiers, software compilation pipelines, container clusters, and general-purpose enterprise applications that benefit from high memory throughput and 64-bit ARM efficiency.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gb.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of memory and a 67 Gbps baseline network interface. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor without bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, the instance offers balanced resource allocation with 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Benchmark results highlight top-tier memory bandwidth, recording 386.95 GB/sec read and 184.61 GB/sec write throughput, accompanied by high multi-threaded scores in Geekbench multi-core (21327.0) and PassMark database operations (47436.59). While single-thread operations and large-parameter LLM processing exhibit modest baseline speeds, the system provides high concurrency and high memory throughput. The instance is structured for distributed databases, caching clusters like Redis, web serving fleets, software compilation, and scalable enterprise services requiring balanced compute and memory capabilities.
